summary: Counting sort sorts integers without comparing them. It counts how many times each key occurs, turns the counts into positions with prefix sums, and places each element directly. Running time is O(n + k) for keys in the range 0..k, so it beats comparison sorts when k is small.

sections.heading: Algorithm
bullets: Find the maximum key k and make a count array of size k + 1, all zeros.
Prefix sums: count[i] += count[i-1], so count[x] is the number of elements <= x.
Place: walk the input from right to left; put x at output[--count[x]].

sections.heading: Why right to left
sections.body: Equal keys occupy a range of output positions. Scanning the input from the end and filling that range from its top keeps equal elements in their original order, so counting sort is stable. Stability is what lets it serve as the digit sort inside radix sort.

sections.heading: Complexity
bullets: Space: O(n + k): the output array plus the counts.
Not comparison-based, so the O(n log n) lower bound does not apply.

sections.heading: Limits
bullets: Keys must be integers (or mappable to small integers).
A huge range k makes it slow and memory-hungry; sorting 10 numbers in 0..10^9 is a bad use.
Negative numbers need an offset by the minimum.

sections.body: Counts for 0..8: [0,1,2,2,1,0,0,0,1]. Prefix sums: [0,1,3,5,6,6,6,6,7]. Placing right to left yields [1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4, 8].

Radix sort applies a stable counting sort to each digit from least to most significant. For d-digit numbers in base b it runs in O(d (n + b)), which can beat O(n log n) for fixed-width keys such as 32-bit integers (4 passes of base 256).

subtopics.title: Bucket sort
subtopics.summary: The related idea for real numbers.

sections.body: Distribute values into buckets by range, sort each bucket (often with insertion sort), and concatenate. Expected O(n) when input is uniformly distributed.
The counting phase alone gives character frequencies, histograms, and anagram checks in O(n), and the prefix sums answer 'how many elements are <= x?' queries instantly.
Subtract the minimum from every key, sort in 0..(max-min), and add it back on output. The count array then spans max - min + 1 entries.

takeaways: Count occurrences, prefix-sum, place right to left.
O(n + k) time and space; stable.
Great for small integer ranges; poor for large ones.
Stable counting sort powers radix sort.
